name: Grace Minseo Han

residence.housing: Lives alone in a modest condo she owns. It is comfortable rather than spacious, with room for her books, outdoor gear, and a small desk where she sometimes reviews maps after work.
residence.household: One-person household. Her parents and other relatives live elsewhere in the Puget Sound area.

gross_household_income.source: All of her gross household income comes from her salary.
gross_household_income.financial_context: She has a stable income and keeps separate savings for travel and outdoor gear. She budgets before trips, but is willing to spend more when it buys her extra time in a place or a guided outing she expects to learn from.

education.credential: Bachelor's degree in geography from a public university in Washington.
education.focus: Coursework in physical geography, cartography, and environmental analysis gave her a foundation for later GIS work. She especially liked assignments that required careful interpretation of maps and landscapes rather than quick, broad conclusions.
education.path: After college she moved into entry-level GIS work and developed further technical skills on the job.

long_term_goals: Build a steady career that keeps her connected to environmental data and leaves room for some field-related work.
Maintain enough financial flexibility to take an occasional longer coastal trip without turning every vacation into a tightly scheduled itinerary.
Keep improving at interpreting shoreline and habitat data, including being able to explain what a map can and cannot show.
Stay rooted in the Puget Sound region for now; she has no fixed timeline for a major move or a different kind of life.

occupation.title: GIS analyst at an environmental consulting firm.
occupation.work: She maps and checks environmental data used in consulting projects, including spatial information related to habitats, shorelines, and land use. A substantial part of her work is careful data review: she notices when layers do not line up, questions ambiguous labels, and documents limitations rather than smoothing them over.
occupation.work_style: Patient and exacting with technical tasks, she prefers a clear project brief and enough uninterrupted time to check details. She can coordinate with colleagues and clients, but dislikes meetings that repeat information without making a decision.
occupation.career_history: Her geography background led directly into GIS work after college. She has grown from handling narrower mapping tasks into taking responsibility for more complex analysis and quality checks.

style: In a new group she speaks quietly and listens before joining in. Once the conversation turns to a subject she knows, especially maps, shorelines, or wildlife, she becomes more animated and precise. She pauses to choose a specific word and will gently correct a species name or a mistaken description if it matters to the discussion. Her humor is dry and understated. She is direct about practical limits: if she is tired, uncomfortable, or being hurried, she says so rather than disguising it as enthusiasm.

personality.scale: Fictional descriptive tendencies on a 1–5 scale, where 1 is relatively low and 5 is relatively high in the named trait. These are character descriptions, not psychometric measurements.

openness.description: Curious about natural places, essays, and unfamiliar details. She enjoys learning how a landscape works, but is not drawn to novelty for its own sake.

conscientiousness.description: Careful with maps, trip logistics, and commitments. She plans enough to feel prepared, while leaving some space for an interesting detour.

extraversion.description: Reserved in unfamiliar groups and more comfortable with a close friend or a quiet evening alone than with networking or large gatherings.

agreeableness.description: Considerate and generally cooperative, but not especially eager to agree just to keep a conversation smooth. She will state a disagreement plainly when she thinks a detail is wrong.

neuroticism.description: Usually steady and not prone to spiraling over ordinary uncertainty. Poor weather or a rushed plan can irritate her, but she is comfortable changing course when the circumstances warrant it.

travel.what_she_wants: She travels to spend unhurried time in coastal habitats and notice how wildlife and shorelines change across places and seasons. A good trip gives her time to watch, take notes, and return to a stretch of shore more than once; she is less interested in checking off a long list of attractions.
travel.companions_and_timing: Her longtime college friend is her closest travel companion and shares her interest in being outdoors. With work to fit around, Grace tends to favor long weekends and occasional trips of several days, rather than frequent travel. For a longer vacation, she would rather add a day or two in one region than hurry between many stops.
travel.transport_and_lodging: For coastal trips in the region, she usually drives with her friend. They share a simple cabin or small rental with easy access to the shore. She values a comfortable place to dry wet layers and sleep well, but does not need a resort or elaborate amenities.
travel.planning_and_spending: She checks tide and weather conditions, packs waterproof layers, binoculars, and a notebook, and makes a loose plan around access and low tides. She budgets ahead, but will pay more for an extra day or a knowledgeable guided outing when it would deepen her understanding of a place. She does not want every hour booked.
travel.past_trip: A memorable vacation was a few days on a rocky stretch of the Washington coast with her friend. They planned around low tides and spent longer than expected observing anemones and seabirds. The trip worked for her precisely because they could linger and let close observation take precedence over their rough itinerary.
travel.time_she_did_not_go: On one occasion, a friend’s work obligation disrupted a planned long weekend. Grace chose not to make the same trip alone at short notice. She stayed local, took walks, and had a quiet weekend at home rather than forcing a substitute itinerary.
travel.what_does_not_appeal: She is not seeking a packed sightseeing schedule, nightlife-centered vacations, or a trip where the main activity is rushing from one famous stop to another. Crowds do not automatically ruin a place for her, but she prefers quieter access and enough time to find her own pace.

preferences.reading: She enjoys reading for leisure and personal interest, especially nature writing, essays, and novels. Before bed she often reads a few pages or a chapter. She likes prose that is observant without being showy and exchanges recommendations with her college friend.
preferences.free_time: She likes local waterfront walks, occasional paddling, and quiet shoreline exploration. She is interested in small marine life and bird activity, but treats observing them as a pleasure rather than a competition or fitness challenge.
preferences.home: A rainy evening alone with a book suits her. She also likes a low-key meal with one or two people more than a large planned social event.

beliefs.political_outlook: She prioritizes individual liberty in both social life and economic choices, and is skeptical of broad government restrictions. She prefers arguments that explain a rule's scope and practical effects over appeals to authority alone. Her work with environmental data has made her value accurate information and careful analysis, but she does not assume that every environmental concern calls for a sweeping restriction.
beliefs.personal_values: She values independence, competence, honest uncertainty, and being able to make her own choices. She respects people who can explain a disagreement without treating it as a personal insult.

skills: GIS mapping, spatial data handling, and careful quality checks.
Recognizing inconsistencies between map layers and communicating what the underlying data does not establish.
Planning coastal outings around tide and weather information.
Patient observation and taking useful field notes.
Amateur identification of some shoreline organisms and seabirds; she is careful not to present herself as an expert naturalist.
Focused reading and synthesizing detailed written information.
behaviors: After work, she often walks a waterfront trail or checks local tide and weather conditions before deciding whether a weekend shoreline outing is practical.
On an outing, she may stop for a long time to observe one small patch of shore. She is content to come back with notes and impressions rather than a dramatic photograph or a high step count.
She usually prepares outdoor gear in advance, but does not treat a plan as binding when conditions change.
She often reads before bed and sometimes sends her friend a brief message about a passage or book recommendation.
When a conversation becomes crowded or repetitive, she tends to listen rather than compete for airtime. In a one-on-one conversation she is more forthcoming.

health.general: Her health supports ordinary walking, casual paddling, and recreational shoreline outings. She is not pursuing athletic performance and does not organize her free time around fitness targets.
health.outdoor_care: She takes cold, wet conditions and changing coastal weather seriously. She brings suitable layers and pays attention to access and conditions rather than treating a planned outing as a reason to take unnecessary risks.

relationships.closest_friend: A longtime college friend is her closest companion for coastal trips and a regular exchange partner for book recommendations. They share an interest in being outdoors but are comfortable spending quiet stretches without filling them with conversation.
relationships.family: She remains connected to her Korean American family in the Puget Sound area and sees her parents for meals and family occasions. She cares about their opinions while keeping her own home and decisions independent.
relationships.romantic_life: She is single and not currently partnered. She is not actively organizing her daily life around finding a partner, and she does not treat being single as a problem to solve.

leisure_interests: Reading for leisure and personal interest, particularly nature writing, essays, and novels.
Exploring rocky beaches and observing small marine life.
Watching seabirds and making informal field notes.
Walking waterfront trails and occasionally paddling.
Exchanging book recommendations with her close friend.
other_facts: She keeps a separate savings fund for travel and outdoor gear.
She prefers a friendly one-on-one conversation to networking or a large gathering.
Her curiosity tends to settle on small, specific details: a change in shoreline texture, an animal she has not seen before, or a mismatch between a map and the ground.
